clue.text: Hot and cold drink will get sign of approval

parts.note: H is the usual abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
to lap is to drink as a cat does

explanation.surface: Someone mixing hot and cold drinks wins a round of applause.
explanation.definitionFit: A single clap of the hands is a small gesture of applause, showing approval.

clue.text: Lots of people gathering together drink audibly

indicators.note: audibly says the clue word is heard spoken, so its sound gives the entry

parts.note: bevvy is British slang for an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Crowds assembling are loudly having a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: BEVVY is informal British for a drink (often beer); said aloud it matches the spelling with one V.
explanation.definitionFit: A bevy is a large group, originally of larks or ladies, so a gathering crowd.

clue.text: Stood by after king attacked

indicators.note: after places the helping word behind the royal letter in the answer

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex
to stand by someone is to support or aid them

explanation.surface: Someone loyal to a monarch and then turned on.
explanation.definitionFit: A place that is raided has been attacked in a sudden assault.

clue.text: Girl one with long slow strides? Much quicker mover

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
a loper moves with long easy strides

explanation.surface: A girl strolls with long lazy steps, though someone else runs much faster.
explanation.walkthrough: The '?' and 'Much quicker' set the slow-striding girl against a galloping horse or rider.
explanation.definitionFit: A galloper is a horse or rider going at full gallop, far faster than a loper.

clue.text: I chew suet, a smashing addition to ham?

indicators.note: smashing breaks up the letters of the preceding words into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone chewing suet suggests a splendid extra for a ham dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashing' looks like praise for the addition but signals the anagram of I CHEW SUET A.
explanation.definitionFit: A béchamel or parsley-flavoured version of this is a classic accompaniment served with boiled ham.

clue.text: Congenital pest speaking endlessly in pub

indicators.note: in puts the shortened word for a tiresome talker inside the pub word

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: endlessly removes the final letter from the word for a pest

parts.note: a bore is a pest who drones on when speaking

explanation.surface: A tiresome talker keeps going on and on in a pub, as if born that way.
explanation.definitionFit: Something congenital is present from birth, that is, innate or native to a person.

clue.text: Bad weather is restricting team playing — very unwelcome message

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the weather word goes round the other piece

parts.note: hail is a nasty form of weather

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of the team are moved about

explanation.surface: A storm keeps a sports team from playing, and fans send a nasty letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Abusive letters or emails sent to someone are the most unwelcome kind of message.

clue.text: Building with special horses, 51, most unlikely to collapse

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals
very means most, extremely
stable means firm and unlikely to fall

explanation.surface: A building for prized horses is described as solid and sturdy.
explanation.walkthrough: A LIVERY STABLE keeps and feeds horses for their owners or hires them out.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a building houses horses kept there for owners at a charge, or for hire.

clue.text: A part of the face beginning to glow, in pain

parts.note: the chin is a part of the face

indicators.note: beginning to takes the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A part of the face starts to glow while hurting.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sore or hurting is in pain, suffering a dull continuous hurt.

clue.text: Film actress opposite H. Keel in 1953, significant time

definitions.text: Film actress opposite H. Keel in 1953
definitions.meaning: Doris Day starred with Howard Keel in Calamity Jane (1953)
the day of the 1944 Normandy landings, used for any decisive moment

explanation.surface: A Hollywood actress from a 1950s musical marks an important moment.
explanation.definitionFit: The Normandy landings' code date became a general term for any crucial planned day.

clue.text: Violent duo out to get a transfer of power

indicators.note: out means not in order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A thuggish pair are ousted so that control passes to others.
explanation.definitionFit: Devolution is the passing of powers from central government to regional bodies.

clue.text: Still and quiet lake with chemical harmful to it?

parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical direction for quiet
acid rain or chemical acid harms a lake

explanation.surface: A calm, silent lake threatened by a polluting chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm and undisturbed water is still, unruffled and tranquil.

clue.text: Plant some powdery stuff in 5, as one might say?

indicators.note: one might say means the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: cornflour is used to thicken white sauce, the answer at 5

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a plant could be the powder in a sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: The '5' points to WHITE SAUCE, which cornflour thickens.
explanation.definitionFit: The cornflower is a blue-flowered plant of the daisy family growing in fields.

clue.text: Appearing before the photographer again or taking a rest?

definitions.meaning: ..., striking a pose for the camera once more

explanation.surface: A model sitting for a second shot or just lying down.
explanation.definitionFit: To repose is to lie at rest; read as re-posing it means modelling for another picture.

clue.text: Clue to a padre being seen here in military area

parts.note: read as an anagram clue, ... (... up) would yield the clue words a padre

explanation.surface: A chaplain is spotted on the army drill square.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse anagram: the answer is the clue whose solution is A PADRE, with 'ground' as the anagram indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: The drill square in a barracks where troops march and assemble is a military area.

clue.text: Designing buoyant structure with sound cladding

indicators.note: cladding covers, so the sound word wraps round the floating platform

parts.note: ding is the sound of a bell
a raft is a floating structure

explanation.surface: Someone designs a floating platform with soundproof covering.
explanation.definitionFit: Drafting is drawing up plans or designs, as a draughtsman does.

clue.text: See 15
I'd set up plan to engage the old woman — I'm a tactful type

indicators.note: set up in a down clue reads the word upwards, reversing it

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

indicators.note: to engage is to take in, so the plan word holds the mother

parts.note: a plot is a plan
the old woman is slang for a mother, MA

explanation.surface: Someone schemes with their mother and boasts of their tact.
explanation.definitionFit: Diplomats are skilled in tactful negotiation, so the word is used for any tactful person.

clue.text: See 8
Mother or saint in a position to honour the dead

definitions.meaning: MA (mother) or ST (saint) is each one half of the word MAST

definitions.text: in a position to honour the dead
definitions.meaning: flags lowered partway down the pole as a mark of mourning

explanation.surface: A mother or saint is remembered by lowered flags at a funeral.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is cryptic: MA or ST is half of MAST, so either is a HALF MAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A flag lowered partway down its pole is flown that way as a sign of mourning.

clue.text: Stars, about a thousand — they may be fighting each other

definitions.text: they may be fighting each other

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the stars go round the thousand

parts.note: Aries is a constellation, a group of stars
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Constellations number about a thousand and seem to be at war.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposing military forces in a war are armies that fight one another.

clue.text: See shelter inside, wanting to have a rest

indicators.note: inside puts the shelter word within the seeing word

parts.note: to spy is to see
lee is shelter from the wind

explanation.surface: Someone spots a shelter and wants to lie down in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being drowsy means wanting to sleep or rest.

clue.text: What NE river is rising, revealing froth?

indicators.note: rising in a down clue reads the pieces upwards, reversing them

parts.note: eh is an exclamation meaning what
the Tees is a river in north-east England

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a river in the north-east is swelling and foaming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is rising' turns the whole of EH + TEES, giving SEETHE.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe is to bubble and foam, as boiling water does, so to froth.

clue.text: Like many foreign goods, I can be brought in as hand luggage?

definitions.meaning: capable of being brought into a country from abroad

definitions.text: I can be brought in as hand luggage

explanation.surface: An item boasts it can be carried aboard as hand baggage.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as I'M PORTABLE to see the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods from abroad that may be brought into a country are capable of being imported.

clue.text: Little son, depressed and not reacting quickly

parts.note: S is the short form of son
low means depressed

explanation.surface: A small boy feels down and is sluggish to respond.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is sluggish to react is slow-witted or slow to respond.

clue.text: Buried under piece of grass is a chemical

parts.note: a sod is a piece of turf

explanation.surface: A chemical lies buried under a patch of turf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buried under' only links: the surface plays on being 'under the sod'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodium carbonate, or washing soda, is a chemical compound.

clue.text: River gets any number cut off initially

indicators.note: initially says the severing word comes first in the answer, before the number

parts.note: to sever is to cut off
N stands for any number in algebra

explanation.surface: A river that receives any number of streams is cut off at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: The Severn is the longest river in Britain.

clue.text: Animals ascend, running over hill, half hidden

indicators.note: over means lying across, so the rearranged letters go round the hill part
hidden says the hill part is concealed inside the rearranged letters
running suggests the letters of ascend move about
half takes the first two of the four letters of hill

explanation.surface: Creatures climb, running over a hill partly out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' rearranges the ascending letters to ECDNAS; 'over' and 'hidden' both say they wrap round the half-hill, so 'hill' is not a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiny anteaters of Australia and New Guinea are egg-laying mammals, a kind of animal.
